issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'Verbal Access' directly conflicts with the combination of markedly disorganized/poorly integrated recall ('Fragmented Pieces') and intrusive, repetitive reliving ('Memory Replay'). Those latter items imply a poorly elaborated trauma memory that is difficult to narrate coherently, whereas saying he can talk about it very easily points in the opposite clinical direction.

issues.item: Memory: Fragmented Pieces: My memories of the event come in disconnected pieces that do not fit together.
issues.explanation: For a mugging/robbery trauma, avoidance of enclosed spaces and religious spaces is hard to justify from the rest of the profile. No trigger, threat, appraisal, or memory item links the trauma to confined environments or worship settings, so these avoidance targets appear disconnected from the trauma-specific formulation and from the otherwise selected symptoms.

issues.item: Avoid Enclosed Spaces: Enclosed or confined spaces
issues.explanation: The maladaptive strategy items are not clinically well-linked to the trauma type or the rest of the profile. After a mugging/robbery, avoiding enclosed spaces and religious spaces is hard to explain from the given memory and appraisal content, especially when no trigger or threat items are present to connect these locations to the trauma.

issues.item: Avoid Religious Spaces: Places of worship or religious gatherings
issues.explanation: Within Maladaptive Strategies, the two place-avoidance items point to very different situational patterns (confined spaces vs places of worship) without any supporting memory, threat, or appraisal content tying either context to the robbery. This makes the strategy node internally scattered rather than coherent.

issues.item: Avoid Religious Spaces: Places of worship or religious gatherings
issues.explanation: For a 21-year-old male agricultural worker with trauma type mugging/robbery, avoiding religious spaces is not impossible, but it is clinically hard to justify here because nothing in Triggers, Threat, Memory, or Negative Appraisals links the trauma to religious contexts. Within the allowed components, this avoidance appears unanchored to the rest of the profile and does not fit the cognitive formulation, where Maladaptive Strategies should be strongly connected to Negative Appraisals and somewhat to Memory. The other maladaptive items plausibly follow from vigilance and intrusive/fragmented memory, but this one addresses a context not represented anywhere else in the self-report.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Life Not Worth Living: I am not sure my life is worth living anymore
issues.explanation: The profile centers on negative appraisals strongly linked to memory and maladaptive coping after a mugging, but 'Life Not Worth Living' is markedly more severe and qualitatively different from the other selected appraisals, which focus on danger and injustice. With no Threat items and no appraisal→threat link in the formulation, this item stands out as clinically disconnected rather than part of a coherent appraisal pattern.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Checking Surroundings: constantly scan environment for signs of threat
issues.explanation: 'Checking Surroundings' is a threat-monitoring/safety behavior that usually coheres with active Threat or Trigger content. Here there are no Threat items, no Trigger items, and no active Trigger/Threat connections in the formulation, so this strategy appears insufficiently supported by the rest of the profile. The other strategies (screen escape, avoid going out) fit better with appraisal-driven avoidance.
